name: Standard smoothing
summary: Four settings that shape the feel from rest, at low speed and at high speed.

intro.text: These are the Standard smoothing system's settings: dynamic smoothing that adapts to your aim speed. They apply when Smoothing is set to Custom and the smoothing button reads STANDARD.

citations.quote: The Standard system provides dynamic smoothing behavior that adapts to your current aim speed.
You can also customize the smoothing system and choose between two smoothing modes: Standard and Classic.
Press the the smoothing button (i.e. "STANDARD" or "CLASSIC") to change modes.

start.text: XIM says to start from a preset: try each to see what feels most natural, because it is preference. Change other values only if you need to.

citations.quote: Both mouse and motion have different presets designed for those aiming methods. Start by trying each out to see what feels most natural to you. It's strictly based on preference.
Always start with just adjusting Sensitivity. Change other values only if necessary.

statement.text: Raise Easing for a smoother start from rest. The cost is response time.

citations.quote: Higher values result in smoother transition from rest but lower response time.

statement.text: Lower Easing for a quicker response from rest. The start is less smooth.

citations.quote: Higher values result in smoother transition from rest but lower response time.

statement.reasoning: XIM states the effect of higher values: smoother from rest, slower to respond. Lower values do the opposite on both counts.

statement.text: Raise Precision for a smoother result at low aim speeds. The reticle feels heavier.

citations.quote: Higher values provide a smoother result at low aim speeds and increases the heaviness of the reticle.

statement.text: Lower Precision for a lighter reticle. Aim at low speeds is less smooth.

citations.quote: Higher values provide a smoother result at low aim speeds and increases the heaviness of the reticle.

statement.reasoning: XIM states the effect of higher values: smoother at low speed, heavier. Lower values do the opposite on both counts.

statement.text: Lower Response and the reticle feels less light at faster aim speeds. XIM doesn't call this smoother.

citations.quote: Higher values produces a lighter feeling reticle at faster aim speeds.

statement.reasoning: XIM states only the effect of higher values: a lighter reticle at speed. Lower values give the opposite, a less light reticle at speed. The guide uses no other word for it.

statement.text: Raise Response for a lighter feeling reticle at faster aim speeds.

citations.quote: Higher values produces a lighter feeling reticle at faster aim speeds.

statement.text: Raise Stability for extra stability at rest, against hand jitter. Motion aim only.

citations.quote: Increase to provide extra stability at rest due to hand jitter and instability (motion aim only).

notes.text: XIM names no preset and gives no numbers for these four settings. Primer gives none either.
If a game requires Simulate Analog Behavior, XIM's checklist says to use a preset, or, with Custom, not to reduce smoothing below the presets.

citations.quote: It's recommended you use one of the smoothing presets. If you are using "custom", ensure you do not reduce smoothing intensity below that of the presets.
